@@ -1182,6 +1182,11 @@ It performs the following operations in order:
   * Adjusts the stack pointer to create the stack frame
   * Conditionally performs a stack pointer swap by executing cspspush sp
 
+For the register save operations,
+store memory addresses are translated and protected,
+and endianness is applied,
+as though the current privilege mode were set to the previous privilege mode.
+
 NOTE: Intentionally, the GPRs are saved on the stack owned by the interrupted context.
 This is done to simplify and accelerate OS thread switching.
 
@@ -1287,20 +1292,25 @@ The behavior in RISC-V assembly is as follows:
 ----
 mipopret:
   mcspspop sp, sp           # Swap stack pointer with msp
+  set mstatus.MPRV          # No direct assembly equivalent
   lr a0, OFFSET(sp)         # Restore a0
   lr a1, OFFSET(sp)         # Restore a1
   lr a2, OFFSET(sp)         # Restore a2
   lr a3, OFFSET(sp)         # Restore a3
   lr a4, OFFSET(sp)         # Restore a4
   lr a5, OFFSET(sp)         # Restore a5
   addi sp, sp, FRAMESIZE    # Adjust stack pointer
-  mret
+  mret                      # Clears mstatus.MPRV
 
 where
   lr is lw on RV32 and ld on RV64
 ----
 
 The order and access size of the loads, as well as the OFFSETS, are implementation-defined.
+For the register load operations,
+store memory addresses are translated and protected,
+and endianness is applied,
+as though the current privilege mode were set to `mstatus.MPP.`
 
 Included in: <<smip>>
 
@@ -1341,12 +1351,14 @@ The behavior in RISC-V assembly is as follows:
 ----
 sipopret:
   scspspop sp, sp           # Swap stack pointer with ssp
+  "set sstatus.SUM"         # No direct assembly equivalent
   lr a0, OFFSET(sp)         # Restore a0
   lr a1, OFFSET(sp)         # Restore a1
   lr a2, OFFSET(sp)         # Restore a2
   lr a3, OFFSET(sp)         # Restore a3
   lr a4, OFFSET(sp)         # Restore a4
   lr a5, OFFSET(sp)         # Restore a5
+  "clear sstatus.SUM"       # No direct assembly equivalent
   addi sp, sp, FRAMESIZE    # Adjust stack pointer
   sret
 
@@ -1355,5 +1367,9 @@ where
 ----
 
 The order and access size of the loads, as well as the OFFSETS, are implementation-defined.
+For the register load operations,
+store memory addresses are translated and protected,
+and endianness is applied,
+as though the current privilege mode were set to `sstatus.SPP`.
 
 Included in: <<smip,Ssip>>
